_note: Narration for the demo video, one entry per chapter of tools/record-demo.mjs (matched by index; the title is a check). tools/narrate.py voices it; tools/compose_demo.py holds each chapter on screen until its line is finished. Spoken by a stock ElevenLabs voice, not a cloned one.

lines.title: WeKaribu
lines.text: Welcome to WeKaribu: we welcome. A small AI guestbook for small tourism hosts, anywhere. Guests write in their own language; the host hears it in hers. In this demo the host is Noor, who runs coffee tours on her family farm in Tanzania. Because of this tool, Noor will hear, in Swahili, within days of each visit, what her visitors loved and what they want improved, and she can thank them in their own language. Today she can't: the feedback is written in languages she cannot read, and the guide who could translate leaves with the group.

lines.title: Three sides of one phone
lines.text: Everything runs on one ordinary phone, offline, with no server and no account. Three sides: the host, a visitor, and the tour company.

lines.title: A three-step guide
lines.text: A three-step guide explains the flow the first time. The host side is one home screen.

lines.title: Try one example
lines.text: Here is the AI. On the phone, it splits each comment into sentences, matches every sentence to a fixed list of ten topics, and reads whether it is praise or a complaint.

lines.title: The home screen
lines.text: The home screen is two lines: what guests said, and four things a host does. The summary is built from sentences a person wrote; the AI only fills in counts and topic names.

lines.title: In the host’s own language
lines.text: The interface follows the phone's language. On Noor's phone it is Swahili, and Sikiliza reads the summary aloud with recorded clips.

lines.title: Details: what guests said
lines.text: Every topic keeps the guests' own words. When the model is unsure, the sentence is marked Check, for a person. Unsure means ask a human, not guess.

lines.title: Thank the guest in their language
lines.text: Thank-you notes are human-written templates in the guest's language, with the meaning underneath. They go out only with the guest's consent, and only when the host taps send.

lines.title: Hand the phone to a guest
lines.text: The host can hand the phone to a guest. Giulia writes in Italian and ticks that she would buy coffee.

lines.title: Analysed on the phone
lines.text: Italian becomes English with a translation model on the phone, downloaded once. Then topics and mood. The text never leaves the device.

lines.title: Two guests now
lines.text: Two guests now. Giulia's wish to buy coffee is counted under products, so the host can see the demand.

lines.title: A photo of the paper guestbook
lines.text: Most guests write in the paper guestbook. At the weekend a helper photographs the page. A text reader on the phone reads it; words it is unsure of are highlighted to be fixed.

lines.title: Results to check
lines.text: Each sentence shows the original, the English, a topic and a mood, and a person can correct any of them.

lines.title: A voice message
lines.text: Guests can also leave a voice note. Whisper, on the phone, transcribes it and translates it to English.

lines.title: Four guests, four languages
lines.text: Four guests, four languages, one summary: what they loved, what to improve, what they wanted to buy. And a report for the tour company with counts only: no names, no quotes, shared only if the host agrees.

lines.title: The tour company sends a booking
lines.text: The tour company sends bookings from its own phone as a short SMS, so even a basic phone knows who is coming.

lines.title: Next week, and the languages to prepare
lines.text: The app prepares only the language packs the next guests need, and deletes rare ones afterwards, because storage and data cost money.

lines.title: Language packs on the phone
lines.text: Our take on localising AI: keep the models language-agnostic through an English pivot, and keep every word a person reads human-written, in their language. A new host language is one translated file, not a new model. Chagga has no small model yet, so the app says so instead of pretending.

lines.title: WeKaribu
lines.text: Trista, who built WeKaribu, once rode horses in Xinjiang with a guide who was the only one who spoke her language. The family who hosted her never learned what she thought of their day. WeKaribu is for them. Try it at wekaribu dot lovable dot app.
